name: Modal
summary: A focused, blocking dialog — confirm, edit, or make a decision — rendered through the shared Modal.
lead: Modal carries focus-trapping, a mask, scroll-locking and enter/leave motion — too much to rebuild as a web component — so it stays on real Ant: antd v6 (React) and ant-design-vue v4 (Vue), both themed once by the shared modalTheme, keeping antd's built-in motion. Two implementations, one DS V3 look. This is the composite half of the hybrid.

props.name: width
props.desc: Dialog width — DS V3 sizes sm 432 / md 536 / lg 560 / xl 640

props.name: centered
props.desc: Vertically centre the dialog in the viewport

props.name: mask
props.desc: Render the dimming overlay behind the dialog

whenToUse.when: the user must confirm or complete a focused task before continuing
a longer edit form or detail panel that keeps page context
a lightweight yes/no on a single control

opinion.note: Give it a clear title and make the primary button name the action ('Delete slide', not 'OK'). Keep modals short — anything with many fields belongs in a Drawer or its own page.
opinion.dsv3: COVERED — antd v6 Modal themed once by modalTheme. Matrix: type (content · confirm/info/success/error/warning), size (sm 432 · md 536 · lg 560 · xl 640 via width), centered, plus closable / mask. Confirm-family types open through Modal.useModal() (the hook that inherits the ConfigProvider theme) — never the static Modal.confirm(), which the DS forbids because it renders outside the themed tree. Verified via Figma search_design_system against the DS V3 ConfirmationModal set (fileKey MwjvUjVI0HnfwD9EwPXRAy) and antd v6's Modal API; widths measured from the component-standard reference (modal|sm…xl).

snippets.label: HTML
snippets.note: Composite has no framework-free element, so its paste-and-run form is a CDN-React page — React + antd load from a CDN and mount on open, consuming the same shared modalTheme. No build step.

codeNote: React and Vue are two real vendor libraries at two Ant generations — they can't share a primitive. They converge via the same modalTheme; residual drift is caught by visual regression.

conformance.$about: Measured by qa.mjs against the RENDERED UI (getComputedStyle via headless CDP). Composite shown as a CDN-React page; the modal is rendered inline (getContainer={false}, open) so the measure reads the real antd v6 modal content bound to modalTheme.
